mechanism: US equity exchanges aggregate time-constrained closing interest into a deterministic single-price auction and disseminate security-level imbalance, paired-liquidity and indicative/reference-price information before the cross. A large signed imbalance relative to paired liquidity can create temporary mechanical clearing pressure. If that pressure is not primarily information-driven, part of the dislocation may normalize after the auction.
claim: A pre-registered subset of unusually large signed closing-auction imbalances, normalized by paired auction liquidity and conditioned on contemporaneous indicative-price displacement using only pre-cross information, may exhibit short-horizon post-auction normalization opposite the signed pressure direction. No economic outcome has been inspected.
prediction: After freezing one exchange/universe, one pre-close observation timestamp, one imbalance normalization, one displacement definition, one execution benchmark and one exit horizon, high mechanical pressure observations should have more opposite-direction post-auction movement than a predeclared low-pressure/control set if temporary clearing pressure exists.
falsification_scope: The frozen expression is falsified if a properly point-in-time, costed and overlap-controlled test does not show the preregistered opposite-direction relationship, or if source qualification shows the necessary pre-cross fields cannot be reconstructed without leakage. A null does not falsify all auction microstructure effects.

decision_map.who_pays: Liquidity demanders whose time-constrained MOC/LOC interest must clear at the closing cross may pay a temporary concession to offsetting liquidity suppliers when signed demand exceeds paired auction liquidity.
decision_map.why_persist: Closing benchmarks create recurring deadline-constrained demand and exchange rules expose imbalance information only shortly before a fixed auction. Persistence is plausible only where residual urgency exceeds the ability of arbitrageurs/offsetting orders to neutralize the imbalance before the cross.
required_data: Point-in-time exchange closing-auction imbalance messages with timestamps
Signed imbalance quantity and paired quantity
Indicative/near clearing price and contemporaneous reference price
Final auction/execution and future prices only after a separately authorized economic test
Cost, spread, halt, corporate-action and auction-collar fields needed by the frozen protocol

frozen_signal_design.clock: One exact pre-close observation timestamp must be chosen before outcome access; only messages disseminated at or before that timestamp are eligible.
frozen_signal_design.pressure: Signed imbalance normalized by paired quantity; exact denominator safeguards and threshold rule must be frozen from source/data feasibility, not returns.
frozen_signal_design.displacement: Indicative/near clearing price relative to contemporaneous exchange reference price using only the same pre-cross message state.
frozen_signal_design.direction: Hypothesized normalization is opposite the signed pressure direction after the auction.
frozen_signal_design.parameter_rule: No threshold sweep, timestamp sweep, exchange sweep or horizon sweep is authorized by this generation.
frozen_signal_design.horizon_rule: Exactly one short post-auction horizon must be frozen before signal-to-return joining.
frozen_signal_design.special_days: Index rebalances and month/quarter-end sessions must be either excluded ex ante or represented as a separately declared stratum; they may not be chosen after outcome inspection.

fatal_risks: Imbalance may encode information and produce continuation rather than reversal.
Published imbalance can be offset or change sign before the auction.
Historical feed entitlement/cost may make a clean test unavailable.
Auction price is endogenous and may be an unattainable benchmark for a strategy conditioned on pre-close data.
Illiquid securities can create apparent effects that disappear after spreads, impact and collars.
Rebalance days can dominate results and create a disguised institutional-flow/calendar effect.

primary_documentary_evidence.fact: Nasdaq documents closing-cross NOII dissemination before 16:00 ET and the relevant auction-order/imbalance structure.
The specification defines timestamped NOII fields including indicative prices, reference price and closing-cross identity.
NYSE documents closing-auction imbalance publication, paired quantity, reference price and closing-auction timing.
NYSE documents a real-time feed of buy/sell auction imbalances.

nearby_but_distinct: Treasury auction concession: issuance/supply concession in Treasury/ZF, not equity closing-cross imbalance.
Crypto order-book pressure: continuous-book imbalance without a deterministic single-price close auction.
Month-end pension rebalance: calendar/institutional-flow proxy rather than exchange-published security-level imbalance.

next_validator_decision.PASS_TO_TEST_DESIGN: A legally/operationally admissible historical point-in-time imbalance source and one deterministic signal definition can be qualified without outcome access.
next_validator_decision.PARK_DATA: Mechanism is observable but historical PIT feed entitlement, timestamps, security mapping or cost fields cannot be qualified.
next_validator_decision.KILL_MECHANISM: Documentary/source review shows the proposed pressure variable cannot be separated from final-auction outcomes or is not operationally observable before the cross.
